chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him, 'How is tayammum?' He said, 'It is one striking for wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath) from janabah. You strike with your hand twice, then shake them off once: once for the face and once for the hands. And whenever you find water, then ghusl is upon you if you were junub, and wudu (ablution) if you were not junub.'

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath required for major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, whose availability restores the obligation of wudu (ablution) or ghusl
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: ritual ablution required for prayer and similar acts of worship
key_terms.جُنُبًا: a person in the state of janabah

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed for wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath) according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of tayammum and its use as a substitute for wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath) in the absence of water. It also states that when water becomes available, one must perform ghusl if in janabah, or wudu (ablution) if not.
